headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Khoj can read personal notes and broad-egress search outputs may be reused by the documentation-only python-cheatsheet, but the pair lacks shared write channels or documented direct…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress, so malicious content in notes or fetched search results could influence downstream prompts. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no input channels, so the pair lacks a direct automated bridge; the plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or reuse of content, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF Khoj ingests attacker-controlled notes or web content into a prompt shown to an operator
IF the operator copies Khoj output into python-cheatsheet content without review
mitigations: Disable or limit web search in Khoj for untrusted sources
Review pasted snippets before reusing them in python-cheatsheet
Keep untrusted notes in a separate Khoj collection
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved passages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and appears not to ingest files or send data onward. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but Khoj’s broad egress means sensitive note content could leave the local boundary if used with external search or APIs; uncertainty favors medium over low.
conditions: IF Khoj is configured to send note content or retrieved context to external APIs
IF personal notes or indexed documents contain sensitive data
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to self-hosted backends only
Remove sensitive notes from the indexed corpus
Turn off external search providers
requires-engineering: enforce per-document redaction before retrieval

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj can read files but cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses; python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, network, or write capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or locking problem in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or git automation
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace
Do not add git automation without locks
requires-engineering: add explicit resource locking if writes are introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved facts from personal notes and documents, and python-cheatsheet is a content-writing/reference agent that could reuse those outputs as authoritative text. Because the pair lacks a documented verification step and the second agent is designed to produce content, A-to-B propagation can occur in default workflows, though not necessarily with direct action-taking authority.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is prompted to rewrite or summarize Khoj output
IF the operator treats Khoj retrievals as verified facts
mitigations: Require a human verification step before reuse
Mark Khoj outputs as untrusted citations
Separate retrieval from drafting tasks
requires-engineering: add source-checking before content generation

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj processes personal notes and indexed documents, so residency or retention issues can arise if those notes are synced to external services; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so it is not the compliance driver here. The pair does not show a specific jurisdictional mismatch, so this is a limited compliance-gap risk rather than a breach by default.
conditions: IF personal notes include regulated data classes
IF Khoj is connected to a non-compliant external backend or search provider
mitigations: Keep regulated notes out of Khoj
Use only self-hosted inference for Khoj
Review retention settings on connected services
requires-engineering: add data-class routing and residency controls
